title: Operating Lines of Credit Late Charge on an Unpaid Interest Bill
content:
On the Operating Lines of Credit, a late charge is owed on an interest bill whose billed amount was not fully paid by the end of its grace period.

## Rule

A late charge is owed on an interest bill whose billed amount was not fully paid by the end of its grace period; it is charged once against that bill, as a fee charge with the late charge fee code pointing to the bill, on the day after the last grace day.

A line carries at most one late charge for a run of unpaid bills: the charge is assessed on the line's interest bill with the latest due date once that bill has passed its grace period with its billed amount not fully paid, and an older bill still unpaid at that point carries no further late charge.

## Business effect

The late charge appears in the line's transaction history as a fee charge with the late charge fee code, pointing to the interest bill it is assessed on, and the fees the line shows as owed rise by the same amount.

## Platform reference: `assess_late_charge_706782fd`

**Capability.** Assesses a late charge on an operating line against one interest bill. One call books one new fee charge with the late charge fee code, dated today and marked as a platform booking, pointing to the named interest bill, and raises the line's fees owed by the same amount.

**How it is invoked.** This is an agent-side tool: the servicing representative unlocks `assess_late_charge_706782fd` and then calls it.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `line_id` | Loan number of the operating line the charge is booked on, as shown when the member's operating lines are looked up | Identifier |
| `source_txn_id` | Reference number of the interest bill the charge is assessed on, as shown in the line's transaction history | Identifier |
| `amount` | The late charge | USD, always positive, 2 decimal places, rounded half up to cents before it is passed |

**Return.** A receipt rendered as text with `txn_id` (reference number of the new late charge), `line_id` (the line charged), `fee_code` (the literal "late_charge"), `amount` (the USD charge, 2 decimal places), `effective_date` (today's date, in year-month-day form), `fees_due` (the line's fees owed after the charge, USD, 2 decimal places) and `status`, the literal "assessed", meaning the charge is on the line.

## Questions on the rule

**Two quarterly bills are unpaid and both are past their grace periods. How many late charges arise?** One, on the bill with the latest due date; the older unpaid bill carries no further late charge.

**What date does the charge carry when booked through the platform?** The call dates it today, the day it is booked.
